THE EMPEROR’S WRATH 

## The Emperor’s Wrath
## **Introduction**
**The Emperor’s Wrath** is an adventure following the disappearance of an Imperial Steam Tank, one of the great technological marvels of the Empire. The search for the Steam Tank will take Characters into the marshes of the Furdienst along the Reikland-Middenland border, where the war machine is immobilised and assaulted by Bog Mummies. If the Characters free the Steam Tank, they may become embroiled in a scheme to steal the pay chest of a tyrannical mercenary captain from a nearby village. They may even end up crewing the Steam Tank themselves whilst embarking on this heist! 

At the end of the adventure is an Appendix, describing how to use a Steam Tank in games of **Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay** . It is best for GMs to familiarise themselves with this before running the adventure, as Steam Tanks are complicated mechanisms. 

## **Adventure Summary**
Ludwig von Uberdorf, former engineer commander of the Emperor’s Wrath Steam Tank, recruits the Characters from his sickbed at the Imperial School of Engineers in Altdorf. Two weeks ago, the Emperor’s Wrath and her crew headed north to reinforce Graf Todbringer’s campaign against the Beastmen of the Drakwald. No one has heard from her since. Von Uberdorf wants the Characters to discover what became of the tank and her crew and rescue his comrades before the reiksmarshal has them court-martialled for desertion. 

Following the trail of the Emperor’s Wrath leads the Characters into the Furdienst, a patch of marshland along the northern bank of the River Reik in Middenland. The tank’s crew are suspicious of new arrivals, but accept the Characters’ help out of necessity. The Emperor’s Wrath is stuck in the mud, and Bog Mummies are closing in to finish off the crew if they can’t get moving soon. 

After escaping the swamp, the engineers cut the Characters in on their scheme. A mercenary deserter has tipped them off about her former employer, who 

has set himself up as despot in the nearby village of Schattenlas. The crew intend to liberate Schattenlas, steal the mercenary captain’s pay chest, and continue on to the northern front. If the Characters sign up to the plan, they’ll earn themselves a generous cut of the loot — and enjoy a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to wage war from inside a Steam Tank’s metal shell! 

## **Steel Behemoths**
Steam Tanks are amongst the deadliest weapons in the Empire’s arsenal: thickly armoured, fully enclosed vehicles, each driven by the piston-pumping power of its internal steam boiler. This water pressure also fuels the Steam Tank’s complement of heavy weaponry, the very best Imperial engineers have to offer. The noise and belching smog of a Steam Tank’s advance are so terrifying that many armies flee at its mere appearance. This is just as well, because Steam Tanks are temperamental machines, liable to break down or overheat in prolonged engagements. 

The Steam Tanks are the magnum opus of Leonardo de Miragliano, founder of the Imperial School of Engineers. Though each tank is a potent military resource, they are also rare and precious technological achievements, and the school is always hesitant to risk them in combat. When a Steam Tank is wrecked or disappears, it is an immediate cause for alarm, and search parties are hastily assembled to recover whatever remains of the machine. In **The Emperor’s Wrath** , the Characters undertake such a search. 

## **The Eight Wonders of the Empire**
Only twelve Steam Tanks were fabricated by Leonardo de Miragliano, and that number has dwindled since his disappearance five hundred years ago. Four of the original Steam Tanks are lost or irreparably wrecked, and all attempts by Imperial engineers to replicate Leonardo’s genius have met with failure. The most promising reproduction, by a rival school of engineers based in Nuln, was thwarted in the year 2499 IC, when the school and their Steam Tank prototype were razed to the ground under suspicious circumstances. Nonetheless, the 

engineers of Nuln are working on a new version known as ‘Old Red’, which has yet to be field tested. 

Tracing the 500-year histories of the remaining eight Steam Tanks is no easy prospect. Each has been repaired, refitted, and rebuilt so many times they scarcely resemble Leonardo’s originals, and many have been renamed to commemorate battlefield victories or improvements made by gifted engineers. The record below is the Imperial School of Engineers’ best understanding of the mechanical marvels remaining under their stewardship.

## **One of Our Tanks Is Missing**
Ludwig von Uberdorf, combat engineer and former Steam Tank commander, requires seasoned warriorinvestigators to help him with a sensitive matter. If the Characters are experienced adventurers (especially if they have completed **The Enemy Within** campaign), von Uberdorf specifically seeks them out. In a letter delivered 

by carrier pigeon, or by a young engineering student, he offers a profitable opportunity concerning the security of the Empire, best discussed face-to-face. Von Uberdorf is currently convalescing from battle wounds within his lodgings at the Imperial School of Engineers in Altdorf. He encourages the Characters to meet him there. 

If the Characters have yet to make a name for themselves, their connection to von Uberdorf could be more personal than professional. 

If they have a friend or family connection to the Imperial School of Engineers, or a military unit that has fought alongside the Emperor’s Wrath before (such as the ‘Grudgebringer’ mercenary company), their mutual associate recommends them to von Uberdorf. Or the Characters may simply be one party of many the engineer recruits for the job — the ‘quantity over quality’ solution! 

The Imperial School of Engineers is forever a bustle of activity. Groups of students, clustered around dormitories and lecture theatres, compete with the adjoining foundry in animation and volume. The upper storeys of the building, where von Uberdorf ’s lodgings are located, include personal workshops of the school’s faculty, and mechanical wonders litter the halls. A clockwork suit of armour jerkily waves at the Characters, before immediately malfunctioning (to its handler’s red-faced frustration). Characters with blackpowder weaponry become an immediate source of fascination and are offered all sorts of dubious modifications. 

When the Characters reach von Uberdorf ’s quarters, the porter escorting them takes her leave. The floor of von Uberdorf ’s chamber is invisible beneath a covering of paper correspondence, parchment sketches, and the refuse of a man who has seldom left his bed in recent weeks. Von Uberdorf himself is a middle-aged soldiering type, with an elaborate moustache, cleft chin, and crossscar cut into his left cheek. His arm is in a sling, and his head is bandaged. He thanks the Characters for their attendance, and requests they speak up to overcome his hearing loss. 

Von Uberdorf introduces himself as the former engineer commander of the Emperor’s Wrath Steam Tank. All but the most unschooled Characters should know what a Steam Tank is — they are renowned treasures of the Empire’s military might — but von Uberdorf can illuminate the ignorant, providing any of the information given previously about the history of the celebrated war machines. Recently he was forced to forfeit his command, after suffering injuries battling Orc boarders at the Battle of the Blighted Towers. 

When the reiksmarshal commanded the Steam Tank be deployed to Drakwald Forest two weeks ago, to support Graf Todbringer’s war against the Beasts of Chaos, von Uberdorf felt confident he was leaving the Emperor’s Wrath in safe hands. Unfortunately, reports from the north indicate the tank never reached the Drakwald. The Emperor’s Wrath has disappeared, and the Imperial School of Engineers wants the tank returned or set back on course. 

Von Uberdorf furnishes the Characters with any information that might aid their search, which isn’t much: 

- The new master of the Emperor’s Wrath is Lena von Zeppel — a descendant of the inventor of the von Zeppel configuration of Steam Tank. She is a capable engineer commander with a full crew of four others at her disposal. Von Uberdorf likes and respects von Zeppel’s team, and is as concerned about their welfare as he is about the Steam Tank. 

- The Emperor’s Wrath was fully operational when she left Altdorf, but Steam Tanks are temperamental devices. It’s entirely possible she’s stranded somewhere due to mechanical failure. 

- He can’t think of a good reason for the crew to go AWOL voluntarily but stops short of denying that they could have done so. Should this prove to be the case, he’d be grateful if the crew were put back on the job, with a plausible, alternate explanation presented for the reiksmarshal’s benefit: ‘No sense in good engineers going through a court martial!’ 

- Von Zeppel planned to take the AltdorfMiddenheim Road to the northern front (if the Characters completed **Power Behind the Throne** , they know the route well). The first stop was at _The Wolf ’s Head_ coaching inn in Kutenholz, just north of the Reikland-Middenland border. Von Uberdorf recommends the Characters start their search there. 

- Von Uberdorf promises that the Imperial School of Engineers will pay each Character 2 Gold Crowns if they can deliver the Emperor’s Wrath to the Drakwald, return it to Altdorf, or provide news of its whereabouts (if it requires salvage). On a personal note, he’ll owe them a favour and a debt of thanks if they rescue his friends too. 

## **Ust Dropping Inn J**
Kutenholz is a 63-mile journey north of Altdorf, a day’s ride if travelling by coach or horseback, but closer to three days on foot. The Characters will find plentiful evidence of the Steam Tank’s passing along the road: paving stones cracked by her weight, deep furrows in dirt trails, and discarded mechanical components. Halfway along, the Characters can stop at the village of Frederheim, and make enquiries at _The Dove_ coaching inn. The serving staff remember the Steam Tank’s recent visit (it was quite the event!) but have nothing useful to report about her whereabouts. The Steam Tank continued onwards along the northern road, exactly as expected. 

THE EMPEROR’S WRATH 

More useful information awaits at Kutenholz. The Wolf ’s Head, an inn sponsored by Castle Rock Coaches, sits at the centre of the village. Its landlord, Erik Gastwirt, is a round, gregarious and patriotic host, proud to welcome outsiders across the Middenland border. He’ll probably mention excitedly the recent visit of the Emperor’s Wrath before the Characters have a chance to ask — he’s committed every moment of the once-in-a-lifetime event to memory. 

- Gastwirt reports the Steam Tank arrived at Kutenholz late in the day, with a crew of five exhausted souls. Gastwirt put them up for the night, and bargained with a local farmer to temporarily empty his barn, so the Emperor’s Wrath had shelter from rain. 

- When Gastwirt returned from the barn, the engineers had been joined by a sixth person. Gastwirt had spotted the newcomer earlier in the day — he wasn’t sure what to make of the woman, other than that she was some kind of irregular soldier, and clearly not from anywhere local. The newcomer made a proposal to the engineers, which they debated in heated whispers. Gastwirt didn’t hear any details. 

Beyond that stretch of the Drakwald, the Steam Tank’s course would take it into the Furdienst: an expanse of swampland that smothers both sides of the River Reik between Carroburg and the Altdorf Flats. Gastwirt warns that the Furdienst is haunted by Bog Mummies, long-dead creatures animated by pooling dark magic, who are utterly inimical to the living. Such creatures are not capable of fear. They would attack the Emperor’s Wrath without hesitation… and any travellers who went looking for her too. 

If the Characters visit the barn where the Steam Tank sheltered for the night, they find armour plating, extra ammunition, and less-identifiable components littering the site, indicating the engineers had stripped nonessential weight from their vehicle. 

Gastwirt offers the Characters a night at _The Wolf ’s Head_ at competitive rates, which the Characters would be wise to accept. They have a taxing journey ahead of them, and such hospitality will not be available for some time! 

- The engineers barely slept that night, instead working on their Steam Tank in the barn. He had complaints from some patrons about the noise. 

- All six men and women left aboard the Steam Tank early next morning. Interestingly, they didn’t take the north road into Middenland, but the west road that ultimately bends south to Carroburg. They didn’t keep to the road for long — they turned south-west, back towards the Reik, taking an untracked route that would lead away from prying eyes. 

If the Characters indicate they are searching for the Steam Tank, Gastwirt may offer additional warnings. This is contingent on the Characters having done something to make a good impression, such as visiting the nearby Ulrican shrine, or spending a lot of money in his inn. Otherwise he keeps his opinion to himself. 

- The Emperor’s Wrath disappeared directly into the Drakwald, ever the haunt of the Beastmen and other monsters that menace Kutenholz with periodic raids. Recently though, the Beastmen have been forced onto the defensive by Graf Todbringer’s campaigning. Gastwirt can’t imagine the creatures reacting to the Steam Tank with anything but fear and flight! 

## **Bogged Down**
Pursuing the Emperor’s Wrath through the Drakwald is not difficult. The Steam Tank carved a path straight through the wood, felling trees and demolishing obstructions. Thanks to Graf Todbringer’s purges and the Steam Tank’s terrifying advance, there are currently no predators in this stretch of the forest, but overly-cautious parties may choose to advance slowly and carefully anyway. If they do, the Characters have one fewer day to search the Furdienst for the Emperor’s Wrath before the Bog Mummies attack (see below). 

After two days in the forest, the Characters reach the more hostile terrain of the Furdienst. Between the subdivided channels of the River Reik lies a misty, treacherous, odious, unnavigable bog. Though the mud tracks of the Emperor’s Wrath are initially obvious, shallow puddles of brackish water soon swallow them up, making it difficult for the Characters to determine their quarry’s route. 

Following the Steam Tank’s trail in the Furdienst is an Extended Test, requiring 8 Success Levels. The Testing Character makes **Average (+20) Track** Tests, which other Characters with the Skill can aid with Assistance. If no Characters have the Track Advanced Skill, one Character 

can make **Challenging (+0) Perception** Tests instead, but cannot receive Assistance. The Characters can Test once per day, and if they achieve 8 Success Levels before the end of the fifth day, will have a chance to help the engineers work on the Steam Tank before the Bog Mummies attack. Otherwise, the Characters stumble onto the Steam Tank in the evening of the fifth day, when the Bog Mummy assault is underway. 

Between each step of the Extended Test, GMs should choose a Character to face a Hazard. Possible Hazards for Characters to confront in the Furdienst include: 

- Swarms of mosquitoes, many infected with bloodborne diseases. The Character must succeed on an **Easy (+40) Endurance** Test or gain a Festering Wound. 

- Pools of sucking mud, much deeper than they seem. The Character must succeed on a **Challenging (+0) Dodge or Perception** Test or fall in. The rest of the party can help them out, but the unlucky Character loses one of their possessions in the extraction. 

THE EMPEROR’S WRATH 

- Cloying mist, which restricts visibility, and confounds the search for the Emperor’s Wrath. The Character must succeed on an **Average (+20) Navigation** Test, or the Characters lose 2 Success Levels from their Extended Track Test. 

- The absence of warm or stable ground to rest upon, resulting in miserable nights of camping. All Characters must make a **Challenging (+0) Outdoor Survival** Test to avoid exposure and take care of themselves — each SL allows a Character to protect an extra person. Exposed Characters must make a **Challenging (+0) Endurance** Test, or receive the _Fatigued_ Condition. 

The Furdienst is not entirely a morass of reeds, rushes, and slurping marsh. Every now and again, the Characters discover a leafless tree, rock formation, or sunken ruin, which helps to orient them in the bog. Towards the end of their journey, the Characters pass the remains of a stone watchtower, curiously intact given its obvious age. Shields are affixed to the crumbling battlements, their faded heraldry pledging allegiance to a long-dead chieftain. 

Characters with the _Second Sight_ Talent perceive the swamp as a sink of dark magic, pooling beneath the stagnant surface around the remains of submerged peoples. With a **Difficult (–10) Perception** Test, those with the Sight can even view magically-animated constructs in the distance, stalking the Characters at a slow but purposeful pace… 

## **Wrath Rescinded**
Within five days of entering the Furdienst, the Characters discover the Emperor’s Wrath and her crew, either through skilful tracking or sheer fluke. The rest of this section assumes the Characters succeeded on their Extended Test, and therefore have a chance to meet the Steam Tank engineers and help with their work before the Bog Mummies attack. If the Characters failed their Extended Test, proceed to **Swamp Things** (see page 14), and read the **No Time for Introductions** sidebar for how to proceed. 

When the Characters find the Emperor’s Wrath, her wheels are sunk deep into a pool of sludge, and it’s clear the vehicle has been stranded for some time. A team of five Humans swarm around the mechanical wonder, attempting to devise a solution whilst snapping at each other and the circling midges. The Characters can listen 

to the engineers debate technical solutions for a while, between recriminations of ‘Told you this was a bad idea!’ When the Characters finally introduce themselves, they immediately attract the attention of the Steam Tank’s whole crew. 

## **A Cold Reception**
The Emperor’s Wrath crew react to the Characters with cautious distrust. On one hand, they’re stranded, starving, exhausted, and under attack from undead horrors, so a helping hand is not unwelcome. But they’re also AWOL, and intent on seizing a prize they don’t necessarily want to share with newcomers. 

The Steam Tank’s engineer commander, Lena von Zeppel, speaks on behalf of her crew. She’s a steely, scrutinising leader, her blistered lips fixed in a polite smile, and her wooden right leg precisely balanced on the uneven terrain. She demands the Characters explain who they are and what they’re doing in the Furdienst. The conversation isn’t going anywhere until she gets a good answer. 

- If the Characters admit they were sent to rescue or assist the Emperor’s Wrath, von Zeppel does not relax — this only confirms her suspicions. However, if the Characters mention Ludwig von Uberdorf sent them, she is visibly reassured. 

- Von Zeppel introduces herself by name and verifies she has been tasked with leading the Emperor’s Wrath to support Graf Todbringer’s campaigns in Middenland. If the Characters point out she is a hundred miles from her expected course, she curtly explains she cannot discuss specifics of her classified marching orders with those outside the reiksmarshal’s office. 

- Obviously, the Emperor’s Wrath has run into problems whilst crossing the Furdienst. Von Zeppel reluctantly admits she would be grateful for assistance removing the Steam Tank from the bog, sooner rather than later. 

The Characters can use social skills to defuse the obvious tension. An **Opposed Charm/Cool** Test against Von Zeppel (see page 13 for her profile) convinces her crew the Characters are here to help, not snitch on them to the reiksmarshal or School of Engineers. Alternatively, an academically minded Character can endear themself by showing off their engineering skill. Persuading the engineers that the Character’s technical knowledge is indispensable is an **Average (+20) Lore (Engineering) or Trade (Engineering)** Test. 

## **The Excavation**
The most pressing concern is to dig out the Emperor’s Wrath and get her moving again. When the Characters have a chance to talk with the crew, it becomes clear why they’re in such a hurry. The engineers have already lost one of their number to creatures lurking in the swamp. The Bog Mummies will be back, it’s just a matter of how prepared the Steam Tank is to move when that happens. 

The Characters have many options to help move the Steam Tank. Some ideas provide only minor assistance but can be attempted with only a single Action — they are a good choice when the Characters are effecting repairs under fire. Other options provide more substantial aid but require a whole working day to undertake. Whether they are viable depends on how many days the Characters spent locating the Emperor’s Wrath. 

Below are suggestions for how the Character can help lever the Emperor’s Wrath out of the mud. Each option can only be selected once, but multiple Characters working on the same option can provide Assistance to the Character making the Test. GMs can use these options as guidelines for any other plausible ideas the Players imagine. 

## **Dig the Wheels Out**
By dredging back all the mud and filth encasing the Steam Tank’s undercarriage, a driver might get the wheels spinning again. This has occupied most of the crew’s attention so far — extra hands would help them to excavate faster than the dirt trickles back in… 

- **Day’s Work:** If a Character spends a day digging out the wheels, the Steam Tank gains +10 on the Drive Test to escape the mud. The Character must also succeed on a **Challenging (+0) Endurance** Test or gain the _Fatigued_ Condition. If the Character is using a bucket, spade, pans, or some other conveyance or digging tool, the Steam Tank instead receives a +20 modifier, and the Character’s Endurance Test is Average (+20). 

- **Action:** A Character using digging tools who succeeds on a **Challenging (+0) Endurance** Test provides +5 to the Steam Tank’s next Drive Test to escape the mud. 

## **Strip the Tank**
Removing weight from the tank reduces the pressure crushing it down into the mud. Most of what the engineers felt they could afford to lose was already ditched back at Kutenholz, but desperate times call for desperate measures. 

- **Day’s Work:** If a Character spends a day stripping the Emperor’s Wrath, and succeeds on an **Average (+20) Trade (Engineering)** Test, they can remove the tank’s steam gun turret entirely, and cover the gap with repurposed armour plates. This provides the Steam Tank +20 on its Drive Test to escape the mud. 

- **Day’s Work (Alternate):** A Character who succeeds on an **Average (+20) Trade (Armourer or Engineering)** Test can spend a day removing armour plating from the Steam Tank’s exterior. For every 10 Wounds the Character chooses to remove from the Steam Tank, it gains +5 on its Drive Test to escape, up to a maximum of +20. 

- **Action:** The Emperor’s Wrath is still carrying enough ammunition to fire three full volleys of its Helblaster tri-gun. As an Action, a Character aboard the Steam Tank can dump one volley’s worth of ammunition, providing +2 to the Steam Tank’s Drive Test. 

## **Improve the Wheel Grip**
Sliding a stable platform under the Steam Tank’s wheels could provide them with enough grip to pull the Emperor’s Wrath out of the swamp. 

- **Day’s Work:** If the Characters recall the shields they spotted on the ruined watchtower whilst travelling here, they can undertake an expedition to recover them. It’s a rush to make it back in time, but at the end of the day, the platforms provide a +10 modifier to the Steam Tank’s Drive Test to escape. The Character must make a **Challenging (+0) Endurance, Navigation, or Outdoor Survival** Test to avoid gaining the _Fatigued_ Condition from their hurried journey. 

- **Action:** If a Character spent a day stripping the tank of armour or its turret, or two Characters have shields they are willing to lose, these items can be placed beneath the wheels as an Action, providing a +10 modifier to the Steam Tank’s escape Test. 

## **Power-Flush the System**
A Character with the confidence to get ‘under the hood’ of the Empire’s most technologically advanced creation could rig up a system to blast through the Steam Tank’s pipes and pistons with high-pressured water. Forcing out all the marsh-gunk should improve the system’s efficiency, and give the Emperor’s Wrath the boost she needs to propel herself to freedom. 

THE EMPEROR’S WRATH 

- **Day’s Work:** A Character spending a day fiddling with the Steam Tank’s plumbing can make an **Average (+20) Trade (Engineering)** Test. If they succeed, the Emperor’s Wrath gains +10 on her Drive Test to escape the mud. 

## **Supercharge the Boiler**
By flipping open all the safety valves, an engineer can generate a sudden burst of acceleration — at the risk of a total systems malfunction! 

- **Action:** A Character operating the boiler of the Emperor’s Wrath can make a **Challenging (+0) Trade (Engineering)** Test to crank as much pressure as possible to the Steam Tank’s locomotive pistons. If the Test succeeds, the Emperor’s Wrath gains +20 to any Drive Test it makes to escape the mud, before the end of the Character’s next turn. A few minutes after the Emperor’s Wrath escapes the mud, her engineer commander must succeed on a **Hard (–20) Trade (Engineering)** Test or suffer a Steam Tank Mishap (see page 21). 

## **Fix an Anchor**
Not far from the sunken Steam Tank is the lifeless husk of an old tree. The engineers linked the Emperor’s Wrath to the tree with the Steam Tank’s winch but snapped the 

chain in one of their failed escape attempts. Characters who prepared for this eventuality might be equipped to try again. 

- **Action:** A Character with a rope or chain can link the Emperor’s Wrath to the tree husk. It costs one Action to securely fasten the link to the Steam Tank, and a separate Action to secure the link to the tree. Once fastened at both ends, the Emperor’s Wrath gains +10 on the Drive Test to escape the mud. 

## **Give It a Push**
If all else fails, a Character can rely on brute force to provide the Emperor’s Wrath an extra boost. 

- **Action:** A Character may push the Emperor’s Wrath from behind — or pull her from the front, by heaving on a rope or chain — to provide a bonus on her Drive Test to escape the mud equal to half the Character’s Strength Bonus. Characters of Size Large or greater provide a bonus equal to their whole Strength Bonus. This is the only option that can be selected multiple times: up to two Characters can push, and up to two Characters can pull, if they have the necessary equipment. 

## **Meet the Team**
Working alongside the Steam Tank’s crew provides an opportunity to ask questions. The Characters will surely want to know why the Emperor’s Wrath veered off course, how the Steam Tank got stuck in a bog, and what the engineers intend to do once the Steam Tank is excavated. 

At first, the engineers are hesitant to confide in the Characters, mumbling excuses about classified instructions. Earning their full compliance requires the Characters to achieve at least two of the following: 

- Succeeding on a Charm Test to appear trustworthy — ideally during the initial meeting in **A Cold Reception** (see page 9), though this Test can be reattempted after a day of working together on the Emperor’s Wrath. 

Schattenlas through the Furdienst, hoping to get back on track to the Drakwald faster and avoid suspicion. Unfortunately, they got stuck. Two nights ago, they lost one of their crew to a Bog Mummy attack. Another one could strike at any time. 

- They fully intend to continue northwards and reinforce the graf ’s war in the Drakwald once their business in Schattenlas is concluded. 

At this point, the Characters may want to cut themselves in on the liberation of Schattenlas — or shut down the unsanctioned operation and get the engineers back on course. Either way, the crew postpone the discussion for now. It’s academic until the Emperor’s Wrath is moving. 

## **Alp Batbayar (Tank Driver)**

- Succeeding on a Day’s Work Action to help the Emperor’s Wrath out of the bog. 

- Confronting the engineers with the testimony Erik Gastwirt provided back in Kutenholz, which already implicates them somewhat. 

When convinced to come clean, each engineer tells a slightly different version of the story, but the basics are as follows: 

- Whilst stopping in Kutenholz on their journey north, the crew were approached by a Tilean hired sword named Alberta Tavella (see page 14). She had recently deserted a company of mercenaries-turnedbrigands under the command of one Matthias Haile (see page 20). 

- Haile and his cronies have set themselves up as petty tyrants in the nearby village of Schattenlas, eating through the stockpile the villagers prepared to feed themselves in winter. They are also sitting on a substantial pay chest, a mix of wages Haile owes his soldiers, and plunder stolen from across the Empire. 

- Alberta convinced the engineers to divert from their course, and bring the Emperor’s Wrath to Schattenlas. One Steam Tank should be enough to rescue the village and get revenge on her former employers. And retaking the village with just a small crew means fewer ways to split up the loot… 

- Since the engineers plan to help themselves to the booty, they couldn’t let military command know where they’re going. They took a shortcut to 

Alp is from Ostland and his Ungol heritage is obvious. He is one of many students from distant lands and provinces drawn to study at the world-renowned Imperial School of Engineers. Since earning recognition as a skilled engineer, he specialises in the dangerous work of test-driving experimental vehicles. Alp is a handsome daredevil who struggles with impulse control — it was his idea to take a shortcut through the Furdienst, though he’s embarrassed to admit it. He needs a cut of the Schattenlas loot to pay off his considerable gambling debts. 

## **Ingrid Von Schrepp (Turret Weapon Operator)**
The steam gun of the Emperor’s Wrath is operated by a red-haired, bespectacled introvert, who prefers to keep a distance from the crew’s squabbling. When at rest, she scribbles beautiful and intricate sketches for new Steam Tank weapon designs. Her latest vision for a turretmounted, multi-distributing, micro-explosive shell projectile launcher could revolutionise the field of Steam Tank warfare, but she needs cash to turn her idea into a working prototype. 

## **Alrick Waller (Main Weapon Operator)**
Helblaster operators tend to have a short life expectancy, but Alrick has survived this far with a healthy dose of restraint and caution. More than the others, he is struggling with the loss of his friend and main weapon loader Hans, who was lost to the Bog Mummies two nights ago. 

lrick is very close to Alp and they often look to guard each other when trouble occurs. He has promised to help Alp with his debts, which are so substantial it’ll take both of their shares from the Schattenlas job to repay them. 

THE EMPEROR’S WRATH 

## **Lena Von Zeppel (Engineer Commander)**
The master of the Emperor’s Wrath is new to her command but comes from a distinguished family of Steam Tank engineers — she claims to have steam for blood. She’s wary and tough, with a wooden leg of hissing hydraulics she built herself. 

She has no need for money and is fully content to just perform her duty of leading the Emperor’s Wrath against the Empire’s enemies. But she knows her crew need the windfall, and out of love for them, agreed to Alberta’s plan against her better judgement.

## **Swamp Things**
Five nights after the Characters enter the Furdienst, Bog Mummies attack the Emperor’s Wrath — this time in sufficient numbers to overwhelm her crew entirely. Hopefully the Characters discovered the Steam Tank in time to help with her excavation, so they can escape before the undead overwhelm them. 

## No Time for Introductions
If the Characters failed their Extended Test to track down the Emperor’s Wrath within five days, fate intervenes on their behalf. The sounds of the undead advance on the fifth night alert the Characters to the Steam Tank’s location. The Characters arrive as the second turn of combat begins, meaning the Characters already have a substantial number of Bog Zombies and Bog Mummies to confront. Since the Characters had no days to work on the Emperor’s Wrath, the Drive Test to escape the mud will be much tougher, but they can still help by taking Actions during the battle (per **The Excavation** , page 9). 

The undead encircle the Steam Tank and attack in waves. With the darkness and the marsh fog concealing their advance, the undead enter combat just 20 yds. from the Emperor’s Wrath, but must appear at least 10 yds. away from a Character. More undead arrive each turn the combat continues, in escalating levels of threat: 

- On the first turn, the Characters are attacked by one or two Bog Mummies (see page 15), and as many Bog Zombies as Player Characters. Bog Zombies are revived remains of the recently deceased — the Steam Tank’s crew recognise their friend Hans amongst the Zombies’ number. Use the profile of Zombies ( **WFRP** page 328), with the _Infected_ , _Infestation_ , _Swamp-strider_ and _Territorial_ Traits. 

- On the second turn, an additional Bog Mummy per Character joins the fight. 

- On the third turn, a Bog Liche (see page 15) and two Bog Mummy bodyguards appear and take command. From this point, the undead fight with more intelligence — instead of surging towards the nearest threat, they gang up on exposed Characters, and actively impede repairs to the Emperor’s Wrath. 

- On the fourth turn, a pair of colossal Fenbeasts ( **WFRP** page 319) crash into the battle, singling out those Characters who are the lynchpin of resistance. 

- From the fifth turn onwards, additional Bog Mummies surge into battle until the Steam Tank escapes, the Characters abandon the vehicle, the Characters kill five times their number of Bog Mummies, or the whole party is butchered and reanimated as Bog Zombies. 

THE EMPEROR’S WRATH 

As an Action, Characters may take a **Challenging (+0) Perception** Test to hear what danger is approaching in upcoming turns, before it lumbers into sight. 

## They Knew the Risks…
The crew of the Emperor’s Wrath do not take turns during this fight, except to make Drive Tests to escape the mud (if this isn’t attempted by a Player Character). Instead, the GM narrates their actions abstractly, as they attempt last minute repairs, or battle the advancing horde. 

It’s entirely possible for some (or all!) of the NPC crew to die whilst fighting the Bog Mummies, and GMs should not hesitate to narrate this unfortunate end for the engineers. Not only do these deaths sell the intensity of the battle, but more pragmatically, they create vacancies in the Steam Tank’s crew which can be filled by Player Characters later. The engineers might even fall before the battle starts — perhaps whilst accompanying Characters on a journey to the ruined watchtower, or assisting a Character who scores an Astounding Failure whilst operating the Steam Tank’s boiler. 

That said, if the Players take successful Actions to protect the crew, GMs should reward that success accordingly. The battle against the undead will not be the only opportunity for NPC crew to be replaced by Player Characters (see **Swamp Fever** , page 16, for further details). 

During the battle, the Emperor’s Wrath does not use any of her weapons, as the crew are saving all available steam power to try to escape the mud. Once per turn, a Character operating the Steam Tank’s locomotion can make a **Very Hard (–30) Drive** Test to repair the vehicle’s Immobilised Mishap. If the Test succeeds, the Emperor’s Wrath is free! Actions taken during the fight, or in the days leading up to it, can provide substantial modifiers to this Test (see The Excavation, page @@). Given that Astounding Failures may result in the Steam Tank suffering even more severe damage, the engineers only attempt this Test after the undead attack begins, when there is no time to wait for additional repairs. 

Once the Emperor’s Wrath is running again, surviving Characters and crew are advised to make their way onto the Steam Tank as fast as possible. Escaping the undead aboard the Steam Tank is not difficult when it moves at full speed, and the Bog Mummies do not pursue once the Characters leave their territory. 

## **Bog Liche**
Bog Liches are the reanimated remains of sorcerers that once inhabited the Furdienst. Their understanding of necromancy was sufficient for them to retain a glimmer of self-awareness following their death. Millennia-long entombment within the marsh’s depths has invested them with a maddened hatred of all life, and their control of undead servants is invariably directed towards this end.

## **Back in the Driving Seat**
After the Emperor’s Wrath escapes the Bog Mummies, a difficult conversation may ensue between the surviving crew and the Characters. If the party already learned about the prize waiting in Schattenlas, and helped the engineers escape from the Furdienst, the Characters are invited at this stage to join the off-the-books mission. Alberta reports her former captain Haile is sitting on a pay chest of 2000 silver coins. Even splitting the loot evenly between all engineers and Characters, it promises to be a substantial pay-day. 

If the Characters met the engineers mid-battle, they will still be completely in the dark about the Schattenlas job. Play out a variation of the scenes **A Cold Reception** (see page 9) and **Meet the Team** (see page 11) once the Emperor’s Wrath is safely out of the Furdienst. Assuming the Characters helped save the crew from the Bog Mummies, they gain a +40 modifier on social Tests made in these scenes. If the Characters convince the engineers to confide in them, they are invited to join the Schattenlas mission. Otherwise, they are kept in the dark, and asked to leave the Steam Tank before it (allegedly) continues north. 

The engineers are tempted to take the risk — the reiksmarshal has already noticed they’re AWOL, and the longer it takes them to get back on course, the harder it will be to explain later. Ultimately, they defer to the Characters’ advice. 

If any of the Characters seem interested in operating the Steam Tank, the engineers are happy to indulge their curiosity, and explain the basics. Characters who receive this tuition gain 1 free Advance in either **Trade (Engineering) or Ranged (Engineering)** , allowing them to make Tests of that Advanced Skill. 

Characters may alternatively choose to spend the journey ranging ahead to scout for danger, planning their assault on Schattenlas, or just focusing on recovery from injuries. 

## Swamp Fever
It is possible enough of the engineers survived the undead attack that there are insufficient vacancies for Characters to occupy aboard the Emperor’s Wrath during combat. Happily, GMs have one more trick up their sleeves: swamp fever! The engineers spent a week trapped in an unhygienic morass, breathing foul air, and swatting away stinging mosquitoes. It is entirely plausible for the engineers to fall seriously ill just as the Emperor’s Wrath is approaching Schattenlas, forcing the Characters to take up their positions out of necessity. Depending on the group’s taste for tragedy, the fever may be fatal, or the engineers may recover after the conflict. 

Again, these GM machinations are not strictly necessary. If the Players would prefer their Characters fight the upcoming battle on foot, they can still make rolls for the NPCs crewing the Emperor’s Wrath as well. GMs should be sensitive to the group’s preferences, and conspire to provide the most satisfyingly dramatic conclusion to **The Emperor’s Wrath** . 

## **If the Characters Demand the Emperor’s Wrath Turns North…**
The engineers are loath to walk away from the bounty at Schattenlas, especially given the sacrifices they’ve already made. That said, they are grateful to the Characters for helping them out of the Furdienst, and would not eagerly choose them as enemies. 

## **If the Characters Join the Schattenlas Job…**
Schattenlas is 42 miles west, another 14 hours of travel if the Emperor’s Wrath sticks to a sustainable speed. The length of the journey can be shortened by risking more pressure on the Steam Tank’s boiler (see **Travel Speed** , page 21). 

How the engineers react to the Characters’ order ultimately depends on whether they expect the Characters to report them for desertion — they will not willingly drive to their own court martial. If the Characters plausibly claim they will cover for the engineers if they 

THE EMPEROR’S WRATH 

get back on course, they bitterly accept. If the Characters offer no such reassurance, the engineers try to escape, on foot if necessary. Either way, the Characters would be advised to personally accompany the Emperor’s Wrath to its intended destination, or the crew might simply turn around once the Characters are out of sight. 

GMs may choose to end the adventure here, or if that feels insufficiently climactic, may improvise one last combat encounter as the Steam Tank journeys north. Many dangers still await the Emperor’s Wrath in the Drakwald, from Gor ambush traps, to Minotaur charges! 

## **If the Emperor’s Wrath Is Wrecked...**
The Steam Tank may have been abandoned in the Furdienst, or break down mid-journey. Assaulting Schattenlas without the Emperor’s Wrath is possible, but much more dangerous. If the engineers and the Characters cannot recover the Steam Tank or get her operational, they’ll have little choice but to return to Altdorf and seek aid at the Imperial School of Engineers. The Characters will get their payment, but Schattenlas remains under Haile’s control, and the Drakwald front suffers a significant loss. On the way home, the engineers scheme with the Characters to get their story straight, or disappear if they expect the Characters to snitch on them. 

## **The Battle of Schattenlas**
The village of Schattenlas is little more than a dozen family farmhouses and a granary, built atop a rare patch of high ground protected from flooding. Wood rots fast this close to the Furdienst, so the buildings are raised on stone foundations, and their roofs thatched with reeds. At the base of the hill, 80 yards from the village, a community jetty affixes a couple of fishing boats, and a ferry that helps travellers cross the Furdienst for a fee. Though south of the Reik, the village’s allegiance is to Middenland, and to Leopold von Bildhofen in nearby Carroburg. Recently stripped of his elector count status, von Bildhofen has more pressing matters to tend to than the criminal occupation of this minor settlement. 

Alberta warns that her former company’s resources are considerable: 

- A small cannon and crew, set up atop the hill with a commanding view. 

- 32 mercenary footsoldiers, a mix of pistol-toting skirmishers and crossbowmen. Alberta correctly predicts that half the company will be abroad scouting or foraging and won’t take part in the battle. The remaining 16 are split between the village 

(8 crossbowmen and 4 skirmishers) and the jetty (4 skirmishers). After a month of eating through the village’s winter provisions, their morale is high. 

- Matthias Haile himself, a wily mercenary commander. Haile has evicted the village elder from her home to use it as his office. The pay chest is hidden inside and will be much easier to find if Haile is taken alive. 

Besides the mercenaries, Schattenlas has a native population of 54 souls, terrorised into serving Haile’s crew as subjects. The villagers are hungry for liberation, but do not have any weapons of their own. Haile will employ the civilians as human shields, if he thinks it will give him an edge. 

## **Approaching the Village**
Schattenlas may be approached from multiple angles. The engineers say that the best way to approach the village is through the Furdienst, to attack it from the east. However, Alberta says that when she left the village the cannon had been placed so as to overlook this route, as Matthias felt that any force from Altdorf would likely arrive from the east. 

Any Character can take a **Hard (–20) Lore (Reikland)** Test. Those who pass may be shown the map in order to decide how best to approach the village. 

## **From the East**
The shortest route to the village is to continue through the Furdienst. The road through the mire is actually fairly good ground for the Steam Tank, having been reinforced over the years with stones and wooden walkways. 

Haile’s cannon is well-positioned to bombard the Emperor’s Wrath as it climbs the hill, but the thick fog that often drifts across from the Furdienst can be used for cover. To fully take advantage of this, the Characters must correctly predict the timing of the fog (an **Average (+20) Outdoor Survival** Test), and quietly dispose of the skirmishers garrisoning the jetty, before beginning their approach. If the mercenaries hear the Steam Tank coming, they will assume that a hostile force is moving against them and prepare accordingly. 

Alternatively, the Characters can rely on speed, pumping as much steam power to locomotion as they dare in order to ascend the hill quickly. If the Characters are unsentimental about demolishing the villagers’ homes, they can gain an incredible shock-and-awe advantage against Haile’s cronies.

## **From the North or South**
The Steam Tank could be driven into the mire to attack the village from the north or south. This will reduce the risk of cannon fire, but the Emperor’s Wrath will have to be driven over a swathe of bog to get into a good position. 

However, to reach this position six separate **Average (+20) Drive** Tests are required. Should any of these fail, the Steam Tank becomes bogged down. To free the Steam Tank a total of 10 SL must be accumulated on an Extended **Difficult (–10) Drive** Test, and actions used to make this Test easier can be employed as before (see **The Excavation** , page 9). 

However, every turn that the crew take freeing the Steam Tank, make a Perception Test based on the Mercenaries’ Perception of 30. If this is passed the soldiers in Schattenlas become aware of the Steam Tank and start to take appropriate measures to prepare for an attack. 

## **From the West**
Attacking from the west is not a good idea. Not only does the Steam Tank risk becoming mired as explained above, but it must be driven through a stretch of woodland. The crashing noise it makes as it does so automatically alerts the mercenaries to the fact that an assault is imminent. 

## **The Pond**
To the south-east of the village is a deep pool that the villagers draw water from. It would be disastrous for the Steam Tank to be driven here. Should the Steam Tank enter the pool, it requires an Extended **Difficult (–10) Drive** Test to a total of 10 SL to steer clear. If this Test is not made within 5 turns, water floods the engine and the Steam Tank becomes irrevocably mired. Freeing it now will be a serious engineering problem beyond the immediate means of the Characters. 

## **From More Than One Direction**
Finally, the Characters may attempt a pincer attack. A small infantry force may draw the cannon’s fire, so the Emperor’s Wrath can advance in greater safety; conversely, the Steam Tank might stage an elaborate distraction at the base of the hill, so that a team of infiltrators can enter the village and take Haile hostage. 

Either stratagem involves greater risk, as the mercenaries already have a considerable numbers advantage, which will be more pronounced if the Characters divide their forces. A small copse of mangled trees, halfway up the hill on the opposite side from the jetty, may provide additional cover to warriors approaching on foot. 

THE EMPEROR’S WRATH 

In any case, Haile’s mercenaries will flee the village long before their company is wiped out. Capturing Haile, the cannon, or the pay chest all trigger a slow trickle of deserters from the fight; this retreat is accelerated if half of the company have become casualties. The mercenaries are more likely to hold their ground if Haile is still around to command them. Haile himself will attempt to recover the pay chest from its hiding place before fleeing the village, but if pressed, will prioritise saving his skin over retrieving the silver. 

## **Matthias’s Mercenaries**
Haile’s crew began life as a Free Company, supplemented with travelling sellswords from Tilea and the Border Princes. They were mustered to patrol Middenland and guard against Sigmarite aggression, an easy job they found much to their liking. With the Turmoil resolved, jobs on offer now revolve around Graf Todbringer’s expedition into Drakwald Forest, much more dangerous work. Most of the mercenaries required little persuasion to follow Haile into brigandry instead, and those that objected (such as Alberta Tavella) were cruelly ejected from the company weeks ago without pay.

## **Tanks for Your Help**
With the battle to liberate Schattenlas won, the surviving mercenaries flee into the surrounding countryside. Cowering villagers slowly emerge from their homes, unsure if the Steam Tank’s arrival indicates salvation. They have already lost so much, and dare not hope for their situation to improve. 

After tending to wounded, and confirming the Emperor’s Wrath is still intact, the Characters can turn their attention to the mercenaries’ pay chest. If they have captured Haile, they can interrogate him and learn its secret location, buried under the back porch of the village elder’s house. If Haile died or escaped, the Characters must conduct an arduous search whilst hounded by the villagers’ pleas, and enduring the nervousness of Steam Tank engineers eager to get back on the road. If the elder’s home was demolished in the battle, recovering the pay chest is impossible within a realistic time scale. 

If the pay chest is recovered, the Characters must consider whether they will share their prize with the Schattenlas villagers. With their stored provisions exhausted, the villagers are unlikely to survive the winter without aid, especially if their homes were destroyed in the fighting. To ensure the village’s 54 inhabitants have enough money to restock and rebuild their livelihoods, the Characters would have to give up the entire pay chest. Torn between compassion and self-interest, the engineers will defer to whatever resolution the Characters’ find acceptable. 

If the engineers have any vacancies aboard the Emperor’s Wrath, and the Characters helped them win the battle, then Characters with the relevant skill set are invited to join the Steam Tank’s crew on an official and permanent basis. If the Characters accept, this could be the start of a whole new campaign arc, in which the Emperor’s Wrath finally joins the northern war against the Beasts of Chaos. If the Characters refuse, the engineers nonetheless promise to put in a good word for them at the Imperial School of Engineers. Perhaps the Characters will get the opportunity to crew another Steam Tank in the future! 

## **Matthias Haile**
A former sergeant in the Middenland state army, Haile’s amorality and selfishness served him well after transitioning into a career as a mercenary captain. His silver tongue attracted a loyal following of Imperial militia and Tilean hired swords, and the tense confrontations of the Turmoil offered a plentiful source of employment. As the political situation calmed, and opportunities for legitimate work became less attractive, Haile switched careers again, and set himself up as a bandit chief. He knows that sooner or later the von Bildhofens will force him to abandon Schattenlas, but for now he’s enjoying the power trip of unconditional rule over a tiny little kingdom.
